packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first read)

Exposure / conduct statement
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text before I read it. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..022 in packet-02. I ran `ls` on the packet directory to get the image filenames (packet.json is in the listing; I did not open it).
- Pencil notes on the parchment itself, visible in the images, read "Stams, StA, Frag. 212r" (image-012/013, face A) and "Stams, StA, Frag. 212v" (image-020, face B). I report them as visible marks only and used nothing from them.
- On sight, the text is plainly a familiar Latin liturgical formulary. That recognition may have shaped how I expanded abbreviations. Below I give the letters as seen and put expansions in parentheses. I did not supply anything that is not on the leaf.
- Beyond the rules: to re-examine four faint areas I made contrast-enhanced crops of image-002, -003, -006 and -007 with Python/PIL in my scratch directory (not in the packet). No other source was used.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two faces, each shown as an opened bifolium (two pages either side of a fold with sewing holes/slits). Face A: overview image-001, tiles image-002..013 (4 x 3 grid). Face B: overview image-014, tiles image-015..022 (4 x 2 grid). Tiles overlap: the same physical line often appears in 2-3 tiles. Each line below is given once, with the tiles that show it.
- One column per page, ruled in brown ink with ruled lines visible. Gothic textualis book hand with large letter forms (about 10-11 written lines per page survive).
- Red ink: rubrics in a red gothic hand ("In ephia", "Infa ac." / "Infra act."). Red or red-touched initials at section openings (A, E, C, P, S, M, Q). One large red initial with a cross inside it on face B left (image-015).
- No interlinear or marginal glosses. No running titles visible: the top line of each page is cropped or abraded.
- Face A left page is heavily darkened and abraded, with a torn lower-left corner. Its last three lines are very faint.
- Face B left page: ruling continues below line 10, but no text is visible there (blank or lost; image-019/020). Face B right page: torn lower outer corner (image-022).
- Later marks: face A right page lower area has pencil "..84" (image-012) and a brown-ink inscription "Ov[...] ... n. 169" (image-013). Face B right page lower area has pencil numerals "1 13 / a 2 b / 6 / 4" and "4/1295?" (image-021/022).

SPANS SELECTED: all surviving text lines on all four pages (about 42 lines). Unread or only partly read: the cropped or abraded top line of each page, and face A left lines 8-10 (faint).
Line numbers are counted from the top of the cited image. Text lines only.

LIMITATIONS
- Physical page order and recto/verso relationship are not established. "Face A" and "Face B" are just the packet's overview order. The two pages of each face may not be consecutive in reading order, since this is a bifolium.
- The top line of every page is cropped or abraded and essentially unread.
- Face A left page, lines 7-9, is too faint for a confident reading. A raking-light or UV image of that area (lower half of the left page in image-001) would help.
- No text was found below line 10 on face B left. A raking-light or UV image would show whether that lower area held text that has faded or been erased.
- Expansions in parentheses are proposals. The superscript-letter readings ("sacᵃtissimū", "Infᵃ ac'", "Q(ui)") are uncertain.
